# luminous_ui — Project Docs & Continuation System

This `docs/` tree is the **durable memory of the project**. It exists so any new
Claude Code session (or human) can resume work **without reloading the whole
codebase into context**. Read this file first, then load only the docs relevant
to your task.

> **These docs are a guide, not a rulebook.** They capture the current best plan
> and the *reasoning* behind it — not a fixed process to execute blindly. If,
> while working, the code or new context reveals a better or simpler approach,
> **propose it**: say what you'd change and why, and (once it's the direction)
> update the affected doc + record the shift in `decisions.md`. The plans exist
> to be improved, not obeyed. What must be preserved is the *rationale* and the
> *update trail*, so the next session understands why things are the way they are.

## New session? Resume protocol

1. Read **`progress.md`** — the single source of truth for *what's done, what's
   in flight, and where to pick up* (the **Resume point**).
2. Skim **`roadmap.md`** for the big picture (the five phases).
3. Open only the **`workstreams/<area>.md`** you're working on, plus any
   **`reference/`** file it points to. Do **not** read the other workstreams.
4. Follow **`conventions.md`** — especially the sub-agent policy and the
   end-of-session doc-update ritual.

## File map

| File | What it's for |
|---|---|
| `progress.md` | Living status + session log + the current **resume point**. Update every session. |
| `roadmap.md` | The phased plan (P1→P5) and dependencies. |
| `decisions.md` | Decision log (why we chose what) + locked assumptions. |
| `conventions.md` | How we work: sub-agents, doc ritual, code/test/commit rules. |
| `workstreams/backend-data.md` | **P1** — Bun+Hono API, tcgdex→D1 ingest, R2 images, auth, deck API, lobby DO. Contains the tcgdex API reference. |
| `workstreams/deck-builder.md` | **P2** — real cards in the builder, richer filters, editor + decks list. |
| `workstreams/simulator.md` | **P3** — the rules-driven game engine. |
| `workstreams/online.md` | **P4** — run the simulator over the lobby DO for real matches. |
| `workstreams/polish.md` | **P5** — profiles, avatars, lobby names, misc refinement. |
| `reference/ptcg-rules.md` | Condensed Pokémon TCG ruleset — the spec for the simulator (P3). |

## The one rule that keeps this working

**Keep context small.** Delegate research, code-mapping, and multi-file edits to
sub-agents (see `conventions.md`), load only the workstream you need, and write
what you learned back into these docs **before the session ends**.

3	Five phases. Each has a detailed workstream doc; this is the map + dependencies.
4	Live status lives in `progress.md`, not here.
5	
6	## Phase 1 — Backend & Data Foundation → `workstreams/backend-data.md`
7	Stand up the Bun + Hono API on Cloudflare. Ingest real tcgdex card data into D1,
8	mirror images to R2, add accounts + auth (email/password + Discord/Google),
9	persist decks/folders, and stand up the lobby Durable Object (WebSocket) server.
10	**Unblocks everything else.**
11	
12	## Phase 2 — Deck Builder & Decks List (real cards) → `workstreams/deck-builder.md`
13	Replace the fixture card pool with the live catalog API. Complete the deck
14	editor (add/remove, counts, format validation, save/load) and the decks list
15	page (folders, CRUD, persistence). Upgrade filters using the richer tcgdex
16	fields (set/serie, rarity, HP, illustrator, regulation mark, ability/attack text,
17	energy cost).
18	*Depends on: P1 catalog + deck API.*
19	
20	## Phase 3 — Simulator Engine → `workstreams/simulator.md`
21	Research the official Pokémon TCG rules (`reference/ptcg-rules.md`) and build the
22	game engine: a deterministic state machine + a card-effect system driven by the
23	imported card data + descriptions. Iterative — accuracy improves pass over pass;
24	unimplemented cards degrade gracefully. The goal is to replicate the real game.
25	*Depends on: P2 (real, usable decks) + the ruleset.*
26

28	Run the P3 engine authoritatively inside the lobby Durable Object so two players
29	on different machines can play a real game. Swap the client lobby transport from
30	BroadcastChannel to WebSocket. Same engine as local play, with tweaks for
31	authority/hidden info.
32	*Depends on: P3 engine + P1 lobby DO.*

37	tracked separately so it isn't forgotten.

# Roadmap

Five phases. Each has a detailed workstream doc; this is the map + dependencies.
Live status lives in `progress.md`, not here.

## Phase 1 — Backend & Data Foundation → `workstreams/backend-data.md`
Stand up the Bun + Hono API on Cloudflare. Ingest real tcgdex card data into D1,
mirror images to R2, add accounts + auth (email/password + Discord/Google),
persist decks/folders, and stand up the lobby Durable Object (WebSocket) server.
**Unblocks everything else.**

## Phase 2 — Deck Builder & Decks List (real cards) → `workstreams/deck-builder.md`
Replace the fixture card pool with the live catalog API. Complete the deck
editor (add/remove, counts, format validation, save/load) and the decks list
page (folders, CRUD, persistence). Upgrade filters using the richer tcgdex
fields (set/serie, rarity, HP, illustrator, regulation mark, ability/attack text,
energy cost).
*Depends on: P1 catalog + deck API.*

## Phase 3 — Simulator Engine → `workstreams/simulator.md`
Research the official Pokémon TCG rules (`reference/ptcg-rules.md`) and build the
game engine: a deterministic state machine + a card-effect system driven by the
imported card data + descriptions. Iterative — accuracy improves pass over pass;
unimplemented cards degrade gracefully. The goal is to replicate the real game.
*Depends on: P2 (real, usable decks) + the ruleset.*

## Phase 4 — Online Matches → `workstreams/online.md`
Run the P3 engine authoritatively inside the lobby Durable Object so two players
on different machines can play a real game. Swap the client lobby transport from
BroadcastChannel to WebSocket. Same engine as local play, with tweaks for
authority/hidden info.
*Depends on: P3 engine + P1 lobby DO.*

## Phase 5 — Polish → `workstreams/polish.md`
Now that user + card data exist: player names & profile pictures on the lobby,
profiles, real deck-cover art, and general refinement. Threads through P2–P4 but
tracked separately so it isn't forgotten.
*Depends on: P1 user data.*

# Working Conventions

## Guidance, not gospel
These docs are a **living guide**, not a fixed process. You have context the
planning sessions didn't — the actual code, real data, what just broke. Use it:
- **Suggest better/different approaches** when you see them. Don't follow a task
  list off a cliff because it's written down.
- When you deviate: **explain the what + why**, prefer aligning with the user on
  anything significant, then **update the affected doc** and log the change in
  `decisions.md` (with its rationale). Small in-the-flow improvements don't need
  ceremony — just keep the docs honest.
- Locked assumptions and D-numbered decisions are **defaults with reasons**, not
  laws. Revisit any of them freely; the only hard rule is *don't reverse one
  silently* — leave a trail.
- Treat file/symbol references in these docs as **point-in-time** — verify against
  the current code before relying on them.

## Context hygiene (the point of this whole system)
- Load **`progress.md` + the one relevant `workstreams/*.md`** (+ its
  `reference/`). Don't read unrelated workstreams or sweep the repo.
- Prefer facts already written in these docs over re-deriving them.

## Sub-agent / workflow policy
Delegate to sub-agents to keep the main session's context lean:
- **Research** (rules, library docs, API behaviour) → a `general-purpose` agent
  that writes a condensed doc into `reference/` and returns only a summary.
- **Code mapping** ("how does X work today, what's missing") → an **Explore**
  agent (read-only; returns conclusions, not file dumps).
- **Implementation** of a self-contained slice → a `general-purpose` agent with
  a tight spec; it edits files and returns a summary + what to verify.
- **Review** before committing non-trivial work → `/code-review`.
- **Big fan-out** (e.g. authoring effect handlers for many cards, or a broad
  audit) → a **Workflow** (multi-agent). Note: user-triggered/opt-in — ask first.

Rule of thumb: if answering would mean reading many files, delegate it and keep
only the conclusion.

## Code & quality
- TypeScript strict; match the surrounding code's style and comment density.
- **Biome** for lint/format; **Vitest** for tests. Run **`bun run check`**
  (tsc + biome lint + vitest) before calling work done.
- Pure logic gets unit tests (see the many `*.test.ts` in the repo); DOM tests
  opt into jsdom per-file (`// @vitest-environment jsdom`).

## Git / commits
- Branch off `main` for non-trivial work; commit/push only when asked.
- Commit trailer per global config: `Co-Authored-By: Claude ...`.

## End-of-session ritual (do not skip)
1. Update `progress.md`: status table + session-log entry + **new resume point**.
2. Record any decision in `decisions.md`.
3. Write anything learned into the right workstream/reference doc so the next
   session doesn't rediscover it.

(`src/index.css` L190) covers just the `<body>` glow transition and the `.route-view` route-fade — it never
touches a Tailwind `transition-*`/`scale-*`/`animate-*` utility on a component. P5-8 modelled the fix

close button's `transition-colors`, the Done ghost button); `Settings.tsx` (the font `<select>`, the back-arrow
icon's `transition-transform` slide, the Back-to-home ghost button); `ProfileSection.tsx` (the Save button, the
sign-in link). **`PlayerAvatar` was already clean** — its only `style` is a STATIC gradient, no
transition/animation (the audit confirmed it), so it needed nothing. **One judgement call:** the Save
**spinner** is a perpetual `animate-spin`, which `transition-none` cannot stop — it got
`motion-reduce:animate-none`. Halting it is correct accessible behaviour (the "Save" text + the disabled/dimmed
button already convey "saving", and `SpinnerIcon` is a 3/4 ring that reads fine frozen), and it is the ONE
genuinely-new variant this codebase hadn't used. **Pure CSS-class slice — no logic, no component, no
API/DB/schema touch;** 1941 → **1941** tests (nothing new to unit-test: `motion-reduce:*` variants aren't
observable in jsdom, and asserting className strings is brittle). engine RULES UNCHANGED (0.41.0). `bun run
check` green (137 files / 1941 tests). Built via an Explore audit + inline surgical edits; **self-reviewed, no
independent reviewer.** **VERIFIED via the SHIPPED STYLESHEET, not a browser drive:** a production `vite build`
emits BOTH `motion-reduce:transition-none` AND `motion-reduce:animate-none` inside `@media
(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` — proving the guards are live in the CSS, not a silently-dropped typo'd
variant (the one real failure mode for a class-only change). A full browser drive under emulated reduced-motion
was judged low-value: the change is purely ADDITIVE and reduced-motion-only (it cannot regress the default
render), and the `motion-reduce:transition-none` mechanism is already browser-verified from P5-8.
**NEXT (resume point):** P5-9 done. **Best next pick — the ROOT-CAUSE follow-up P5-9 deliberately left:** the
shared `glass.ts` button constants (`GLASS_GHOST_BUTTON`, `GLASS_ACCENT_BUTTON`, `GLASS_HUD_BUTTON`,
`GLASS_NEUTRAL_BUTTON`, `GLASS_DIALOG_GHOST_BUTTON`, `GLASS_FILTER_TOGGLE`, `GLASS_INPUT`) ALL carry
`transition-all`/`transition-colors` + `active:scale-95` with NO reduced-motion guard and feed EVERY glass
button app-wide (auth, lobby HUD, filters, decks), so the same defect P5-9 patched on three surfaces still

additive edit — deferred here only because it reverses D88's "patch at the call site" placement and reaches
well beyond the P5 surfaces this slice was scoped to (a deliberate app-wide reduced-motion pass, worth doing).

`db:migrate:remote`). See D89 + `workstreams/polish.md`. Below: the P5-8 header (kept for continuity).

(2) The pin may be a **Trainer or an Energy** while the derived default stays Pokémon-only: guessing needs a rule, choosing does not, and a signature Supporter is a legitimate face. Pure CSS-class slice — no logic, component, or API/DB/schema touch; 1941 → 1941 tests (nothing new to unit-test: `motion-reduce:*` variants aren't observable in jsdom and asserting className strings is brittle). `bun run check` green (137 files / 1941 tests); engine rules unchanged (0.41.0). **Verified via the shipped stylesheet, not a browser drive:** a production `vite build` emits BOTH `motion-reduce:transition-none` and `motion-reduce:animate-none` inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`, proving the guards are live and not a silently-dropped typo'd variant — the one real failure mode for a class-only change; a full browser drive was judged low-value since the change is purely additive + reduced-motion-only (it cannot regress the default render) and the `transition-none` mechanism is already browser-verified from P5-8. **Deliberately deferred (the D89 resume point):** the ROOT CAUSE — the shared `glass.ts` button constants (`GLASS_GHOST_BUTTON`, `GLASS_ACCENT_BUTTON`, `GLASS_HUD_BUTTON`, `GLASS_NEUTRAL_BUTTON`, `GLASS_DIALOG_GHOST_BUTTON`, `GLASS_FILTER_TOGGLE`, `GLASS_INPUT`) all carry `transition-*` + `active:scale-95` with no reduced-motion guard and feed EVERY glass button app-wide, so the same defect still lives outside the P5 surfaces; adding `motion-reduce:transition-none` INTO those constants would fix the whole app in one additive edit, but it reverses this decision's call-site placement and reaches well beyond the P5 scope, so it's a deliberate app-wide pass worth the user's nod. *Why: the resume point scoped this to the three P5 surfaces and D88 set the call-site precedent; honouring that keeps the slice small, low-risk and non-reversing, while the root-cause `glass.ts` fix is flagged loudly as the natural, bigger follow-up rather than silently smuggled into a "P5 surfaces" slice.* (2026-07-27) |

# Decisions & Locked Assumptions

## Product / architecture decisions
| # | Decision | Choice |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Backend data strategy | Own DB — ingest tcgdex → Cloudflare D1, serve our own API |
| D2 | Accounts & persistence | Full accounts + auth; users own their decks |
| D2a | Auth methods | Email + password **and** social OAuth (Discord + Google) |
| D3 | Catalog scope | Full-history-capable schema, ingest SV-era first |
| D4 | Card images | Mirror into R2, serve from our domain |
| D5 | Card type | Unify — one canonical `Card`; builder/playmat are view projections |
| D6 | Online lobby server | In scope — real Durable Object (WebSocket) lobby |
| D7 | Game engine placement | Separate **`packages/engine`** (pure logic) — imported by both `apps/web` (local play) and `apps/api` (authoritative DO). *Why: the engine runs in two runtimes; an app can't import another app.* |
| D8 | Card-effect modeling | **Composable, data-driven op programs** over shared archetype templates (not per-card functions); engine emits **semantic events** consumed by the animation layer. *Why: cards are minor variations on a few archetypes; keeps authoring + animation cheap. Detail in `workstreams/simulator.md`.* |
| D9 | Image mirroring & ingest execution (refines D4/§3.4) | Images mirror into R2 **lazily** — a Worker route (`GET /assets/…`) serves from R2 and on miss fetches tcgdex origin, stores, streams; catalog rows keep tcgdex **origin** URLs. Card-data backfill runs as a **local Bun script** applying batched upsert SQL via `wrangler d1 execute`; a future cron does small in-Worker deltas only. *Why: a full SV backfill is ~10k images — over Worker subrequest limits in one shot and hours of CLI puts; cache-aside mirrors exactly what's viewed and stays within limits.* (2026-07-09) |
| D10 | M9 catalog search shape (refines D5/§6) | `CardBrief` **extended** with `types/hp/regulationMark/stage/trainerType/energyType` (card-table columns only — **no set join**, so no `setName`); `GET /cards` gains **repeatable `type`/`rarity`** (OR within a dimension) and **`sort=name\|hp-desc\|set`**; KV cache keys version-prefixed (`catalog:v2:`) so a shape change can't serve stale briefs. The builder consumes briefs through one adapter (`src/features/builder/catalog.ts` — accented `"Pokémon"`, stage/trainerType/energyType → the single `subtype`). *Why: the grid/filters/deck-math need those fields per tile; per-tile full-Card fetches or a fixture pool were the alternatives.* (2026-07-13) |
| D11 | M9 scope trims (pending P2) | **Kinds** (`subtypes`) filter stays a client-side per-page heuristic (server can't express OR across stage/trainerType; EX/Mega are name-regexes until structured data — P2 tasks 8-9). **Manual deck/folder reorder is session-only** (no position field in the schema — P2 task 17). **Folder delete keeps the lift-up UX client-side** (child PATCHes before DELETE) over the server's cascade semantics. **`RARITIES` is a hardcoded tcgdex vocabulary snapshot** in the rail. *Why: each would widen M9's already-large surface; all four are logged with their fixes in `workstreams/deck-builder.md`.* (2026-07-13) **Revised 2026-07-14 (P2-M1):** kinds now filter **server-side** (repeatable `stage`/`trainerType`/`energyType`) — only EX/Mega remain a client-side name-regex post-filter (tcgdex `suffix` not persisted; follow-up logged); hardcoded vocabularies replaced by **`GET /facets`**. Reorder (task 17) and lift-up remain as decided. **Revised again 2026-07-14 (task 17):** reorder is now persisted — see D13; only the lift-up trim still stands. |
| D12 | P2-M1 catalog surface & legality source of truth | `GET /cards` gains **repeatable `id`** (≤100, deck hydration in ONE call; chunked IN + in-memory ordering twin of the SQL sort), **`nameExact`** (case-insensitive whole-name equality), `serie`, `illustrator`, `text` (LIKE over ability/attack JSON), plus the kind params above; **`GET /facets`** serves the filter vocabularies (7 DISTINCTs, one db.batch, KV-cached). `CardBrief` += **`legal {standard,expanded}`**; KV namespace → **`catalog:v3:`**, with KV **bypassed** for >512-byte keys and any `?id=` request (per-deck id sets never recur — caching them is pure write waste). Web: **`Format.legalFlag`** keys BOTH the `legalOnly` filter (`legal=<flag>`) and `isLegalInFormat` (structured verdict beats printed mark; mark check only for legal-less fixtures) — one legality definition for grid + validator. Deck rules: **Radiant = 1 per deck total** (like ACE SPEC; official rule), Prism Star = 1 per name. *Why: filters needed server truth for correct totals; hydration was an N-request fan-out; legality had two disagreeing definitions.* (2026-07-14) |
| D13 | Manual-order persistence model (P2 task 17) | `position` INTEGER on `decks` and `folders` — **global per user, not per folder**: the web grid's flat array (position-ascending) IS the manual order, per-view filtering preserves relative order, and a nest move keeps the row's slot (folderId changes, position doesn't) — exactly the client's existing semantics. Creates take **min−1** (new rows prepend); migration 0003 backfills existing rows in the old name-order so nothing visibly moves. A reorder permutes the in-view rows **among their own slots' position values** (`applyReorder` returns the rewritten array + the changed `{id, position}` pairs) and persists via **`POST /decks/reorder` / `/folders/reorder`** — absolute assignments, ≤500 rows, applied atomically in one db.batch; unknown/foreign ids → 400 naming them; failure recovery is **resync**, not per-row rollback (the folder-delete precedent). Reorder deliberately does NOT bump `updated`. *Why: slot-permutation keeps payloads at the size of the move (not the scope), needs no renumbering pass ever, and one atomic endpoint beats N racing PATCHes.* (2026-07-14) |

| D14 | Engine core contract (P3-M1) | **`applyAction(state, action) → {ok:true, state, events} | {ok:false, error}`** — one reducer, never throws, never mutates. `GameState` is plain JSON (the mulberry32 `rngState` lives **inside** it, so same seed + same actions replay identically); card instances are **uids** (`"p1#0"`) over an injected `cardPool` carried in the state (keeps `applyAction` a pure 2-arg pair and snapshots self-contained). Seats **`p1`/`p2` are labels, not turn order** — the coin winner *chooses* first via an action, `firstPlayer` records it. **Choices are actions; mandatory steps auto-resolve** inside the reducer (mulligan redraws, prize setting, the turn-start draw), so a `Phase` exists only where a player owes a decision. **Events are the animation + wire contract** (semantic, serializable, payloads always copied — never aliasing state or the caller's action). **Wire-safety:** TS types are not input validation — P4 decodes actions from clients, so every index/seat/count an action carries is runtime-checked (three real card-destroying bugs came from exactly this: a JSON string `"1"` bench index). *Why: the engine runs in two runtimes (web local play + the authoritative DO), and an authoritative server needs a total, replayable, non-throwing function of (state, action).* (2026-07-14) |
| D15 | Mulligan compensation (rules correction) | Each player may draw 1 card **per opponent mulligan**, and **mulliganing yourself does not forfeit it** — so **both** seats can be owed at once (each off the other's count). `reference/ptcg-rules.md` §3.5 previously read "the non-mulliganing player", which the M1 engine implemented as an exemption that does not exist; the reference doc is corrected and the phase now carries a per-seat `owed`/`decided` map. The compensation draw is **clamped** so a player can never draw below the 6 cards they must still set aside as prizes. *Why: a wrong rule in the spec propagated straight into the engine — the reference doc is the source of truth and had to be fixed at the source.* (2026-07-14) |
| D16 | M2 staged turn tail, KO interrupts & damage modifiers (P3-M2) | The turn tail is a **`pending: PendingStage[]` queue** on `GameState`, drained by `advance()` (flow.ts): automatic stages run, decision stages either **park** (phase becomes the matching `ko:takePrizes`/`ko:promote` interrupt, prompt event emitted) or **auto-resolve** when only one legal resolution exists. `attack` seeds `takePrizes`+`promote` ahead of the shared `turnTail(seat)` triple. The parked phase mirrors `pending[0]` (dual encoding, kept deliberately for M2): handlers cross-check the two and reject with **`PHASE_DESYNC`** on mismatch. Win evaluation lives in ONE place — the shared `resolvePrizesAndResume`/`resolvePromotionAndResume` helpers used by both the action handlers and advance's auto-resolves. `gameOver` carries **`GameOutcome`** (`win {winner, reason}` \| `tie {reasons}`); sudden death is surfaced as `tie`, not played out. Printed weakness/resistance parse to a **`DamageModifier {op: multiply\|add\|subtract, amount}`** (×N / +N / −N; unknown garble keeps modern-era ×2/−30 defaults) applied weakness→resistance, floor 0 (§8.5); `DAMAGE_DEALT` carries the modifiers so animators can show the math. Data gaps never guess a KO: `hp ≤ 0` reads as the null data gap. *Why: KO resolution must pause mid-tail for player choices, M3's checkup KOs reuse the same interrupts, and additive legacy weakness ("+20", schema-documented) was being silently misread as ×2.* (2026-07-16) |
| D17 | Engine→playmat projection contract (P3) | **`projectGameState(state, viewerSeat) → GameProjection`** (`src/features/game/projection.ts`): `{ board, piles, pokemon, turn, activePlayer, waitingOn, pendingDecision, outcome }` — `board` is a drop-in playmat `BoardState` (`you` = viewer); the wrapper carries what BoardState can't (`piles` deckCount/discard, `pokemon` = per-uid `{damage, hp}`, `outcome` per-viewer win/tie). **`activePlayer` = turn owner; `waitingOn` = the seat that must act NOW** — the split exists because during `ko:promote` the actor is the NON-turn player (the KO'd defender), and a UI gating on turn ownership alone soft-locks. Hidden info is redacted structurally: opponent hand = positional backs (`opponent-hand-N`, no uids — a uid is stable across zones and would let a client track a hidden card), both prize piles = counts only, decks = counts. Public cards key off the engine **uid** so the Pixi layer animates a card as one object across projections. The phase mapping is an **exhaustive switch** (`satisfies never`) — a new engine phase is a compile error, not a silent guess. *Why: this is the same per-viewer filter P4's server will apply; building it client-side first pins the contract with tests.* (2026-07-16) **Revised 2026-07-17 (wire-up review):** during any `setup:*` phase the OPPONENT's active/bench also project as face-down backs (positional `-hidden` ids, no `pokemon` rows — a row would leak the uid key + printed HP); a hot-seat viewer flip at Ready was exposing the first player's face-down placements. Reveal re-keys positional→uid (remount, not flip) — the same trade as hand backs. |

| D18 | Local play page & engine card-pool sourcing (P3 wire-up) | **`/play`** is a hot-seat local match: `GamePage` owns `GameState` via `useLocalGame` (pure reducer over `applyAction`), renders `projectGameState` through the extracted presentational **`PlaymatView`** (the `/simulator` mock, retitled "Sandbox", is a thin wrapper driver), and the **viewer follows `waitingOn`** for the device flip. The engine `cardPool` is built client-side by **fanning out `GET /cards/:id`** (`src/features/game/cardPool.ts`, concurrency 8, module-level promise cache; 404s cache as stable `missing`, rejections self-evict) — NOT via the brief-returning batch route. *Why: `CardBrief` deliberately omits the combat blobs (attacks/weakness/retreat) the engine reads; the per-id route already serves the full canonical Card KV-cached, and this needed no api change while api deploys stay user-gated. A `?full` batch param is the logged follow-up to bundle with the next deploy.* (2026-07-17) |
| D19 | Drop-legality is a driver-supplied predicate (P3 wire-up review) | `AnimatedCardsLayer` takes an optional **`PlacementPredicate`** (defaults to the sandbox's `canPlace`, so the mock is untouched); `/play` supplies `gamePlacementPredicate(game, viewerSeat)` — a deliberately **coarse, gesture-class** gate (phase-aware: what CAN ever map to an action) kept in lockstep with `moveToAction` by a property test (every afforded drop translates to a non-null action). Fine-grained legality stays with `applyAction` + the error pill. Hand→hand reorder is rejected on /play (the engine owns hand order; affording it was a silent lie). *Why: the phase-unaware mock `canPlace` afforded gestures the engine could never accept (accept-animation → wrong-rule error pill), and M4 evolve/trainer drags can't be expressed through it — the seam had to move to the driver.* (2026-07-17) |
| D20 | Text-derived attack effects (P3-M3) | Status-applying attacks resolve through a **conservative exact-sentence deriver** (`packages/engine/src/effects.ts`): five anchored whole-effect patterns ("Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now {X}.", the coin-flip-gated variant, "This Pokémon is now {X}.", the Rest heal compound, the raised-poison Checkup variant) compile to a tiny **`EffectStep[]`** program (applyStatus/heal/coinFlipGate) executed after damage, before the KO check; ANY other text keeps today's loud `ATTACK_EFFECT_SKIPPED`. This is the first sliver of D8's op-program system — M4's id-keyed registry will sit ABOVE it (`programFor(cardId) ?? derive(text)`), and the interpreter is deliberately still attack-private until M4's ops force its real shape. **Self-`Paralyzed` is excluded from the self-pattern**: official wording clears paralysis only if "Paralyzed since the beginning of your last turn", so self-paralysis at your own turn's end must SURVIVE the immediate checkup — our blanket ended-seat clear (correct for every opponent-inflicted case) would wrongly erase it, so the deriver refuses the sentence until paralysis carries an applied-turn stamp; `reference/ptcg-rules.md` §12/§13.4 corrected at the source (the D15 precedent). Demo decks swapped in real status attackers (Numel sv03-031 ×3 Fire/Burn, Luvdisc sv02-047 ×3 Water/Asleep) so /play exercises the pipeline. *Why: statuses without an application path are dead code until M4; exact-sentence matching makes dozens of real cards fully simulated with zero guessing, and the apostrophe class (`['’]`) is the only tolerance so a re-ingest can't silently un-derive them.* (2026-07-17) |
| D21 | Battle state rides the CardModel (P3-M3 surface) | `CardModel` gains **`battle?: {damage, hp, conditions}`**, attached by the projection to in-play Pokémon only — the `statuses` side-table (`GameProjection.pokemon`, prop-drilled 5 hops to DamageChip) is DELETED; chips (damage + the new SLP/PAR/CNF/BRN/PSN pills) read the card they decorate. The playmat stays engine-free: `BattleConditions` is a structural restatement of the engine's `SpecialConditions`, pinned by a **two-way compile-time assignability assert** in `battleStateOf` (an added engine condition field fails the build instead of silently never rendering); `conditions` is REQUIRED (`NO_CONDITIONS` const for mocks) so a missing object can't read as "no conditions" downstream. The checkup itself runs entirely inside `advance` — **no new Phase members**; its KOs park on the existing ko:* interrupts, and the projection reports **`activeSeat: null` for between-turns parks** (discriminated by the pending queue: an in-turn KO still carries its endTurn/checkup tail, a checkup KO has drained it to bare startTurn). *Why: the side-table was the wire-up review's known wart; co-location kills the drilling, and the vocabulary stays out of the playmat per the zero-engine-imports rule — lift it to `@luminous/schema` when M4 markers force the shape to grow.* (2026-07-17) |

| D23 | Trainers + Abilities via a resumable effect interpreter (P3-M4 slice 2) | The real first appearance of D8's op-program system (D20's deriver was "the first sliver"). **One shared interpreter** (`packages/engine/src/interpreter.ts`) runs every op program — attacks, Trainers, Abilities alike; the M3 attack-private `runEffectSteps` is GONE. Representative set only — 6 Trainers (Professor's Research / Nest Ball / Boss's Orders / Switch / Potion / Energy Search) + 2 Abilities (Chien-Pao ex *Shivery Chill* activated, Bouffalant *Bouffer* passive), real sv01–sv03 ids in the demo decks; **broad SV-pool coverage is a later Workflow fan-out that just adds registry rows.** engineVersion 0.5.0. *Why: the M3 traps predicted exactly this — the registry sits above the deriver, and the interpreter had to be RESTRUCTURED (not extracted) to gain mid-effect parking + non-Active targets. Doing Trainers AND Abilities together proved the one interpreter serves both trigger models (play-a-card vs use-an-ability) and the passive-hook path, so the shape is validated before scale.* (2026-07-17) |
| D24 | Persistent-zone Trainers via a continuous-modifier pipeline (P3-M4 slice 3) | Stadiums (§7.3) and Pokémon Tools (§7.4) don't run op **programs** — their effects are **continuous**, so a new module **`packages/engine/src/continuous.ts`** aggregates them and is the ONE place a rule read consults them: `effectiveRetreatCost` (turn.ts retreat), `effectiveAttackCost` (attack.ts cost check), `effectiveMaxHp` (flow.ts `isLethallyDamaged` — the KO test — and the web `battle.hp`), and `passivesOf` (attack.ts damage: a defender's post-W/R reduction — now Bouffalant "Bouffer" **and** a defending Tool — plus an attacker's pre-W/R bonus). **Stadium** is a single shared **`GameState.stadium` {uid, owner}**: `playTrainer` routes Stadiums to `playStadium` (one/turn via a new `stadiumPlayed` allowance; replace-on-play discards the predecessor to **its owner's** pile; the same-**NAME** ban compares names not ids, so the sv02-171/sv03-229 "Artazon" reprints can't self-replace); allowed on turn 1 (§4 bans only Supporters + attacking). **Tool** is a new action **`attachTool`** (NOT playTrainer — it carries a target): one per Pokémon, uncapped per turn, no allowance consumed, no detach — it rides the stack through evolution and discards with a KO'd stack (the `tools` slot M1 reserved is finally populated). Both a Stadium and a Tool with NO authored `stadium`/`passive` row reject loudly (`TRAINER_NOT_SIMULATED`) — the coverage strategy, not a silent no-op. Representative set: Beach Court (sv01-167, Basic retreat −1) + Pokémon League HQ (sv03-192, Basic attacks +{C}) + Vitality Band (sv01-197, +10 before W/R) + Bravery Charm (sv02-173, Basic +50 HP). **Web:** Stadiums are BOTH a HUD button and a drag onto the shared stadium slot (`moveToAction`/`gamePlacementPredicate` gained the `owner:"global" zone:"stadium"` exception — the one non-own drop target); Tools attach by drag onto an own Pokémon (the energy-attach gesture). An Active in that state is cleaned up at the next Checkup; a benched one is not (the same Active-only KO limit bench spread damage already carries). A mid-turn KO that RESUMES the actor's turn is new flow machinery, deferred with the bench-KO generalization; pinned by a characterization test. *Why: Stadium/Tool effects are continuous reads, not the interpreter's mid-effect programs, so a pipeline module — not registry op arrays — is the right seam, and it unifies the passive hook D23 introduced (Tools and printed passives feed one read site).* (2026-07-18) |
| D25 | Knock Out generalized off the Active (P3-M4 slice 4) | The KO flow was **Active-only + turn-ending**; two reaches needed it generalized. (2) **`collectKnockOuts(state, seats, events)`** is the ONE post-damage sweep — every lethally-damaged in-play Pokémon (Active + Bench), prizes to each KO'd side's opponent (`otherSeat`, universal per §8.1), stages grouped **prizes-first**, and the §14 **tie guard runs only when both seats lost a Pokémon** (a one-sided batch only ever wins for the one player) via the same speculative `evaluateWin`. It replaces the inline KO blocks in `attack.ts finishAttack` (now sweeps the defender's WHOLE board — the Active from base damage AND any sniped Bench) and `flow.ts runCheckup`, so §14 precedence stays single-sourced. (3) **A new `PendingStage {kind:"resumeTurn"; seat}` + `resolveMidTurnKnockOuts`**: a KO mid-turn (not from an attack) resolves its prize/promote stages then **RESUMES** the actor's turn (phase back to `turn:action`) instead of ending it — allowances live on `GameState`, untouched by the interrupt. This closes D24's **deferred evolve-below-HP gap**: `evolve` now runs the KO check, so a benched charmed Basic that evolves below the new stage's HP (a Bravery Charm's Basic-only +50 dropping off — the one effect that LOWERS effective max HP) is Knocked Out the instant it evolves, mid-turn, with the opponent taking the prize on the actor's turn. (4) **A `spreadDamage` op** (`{op:"spreadDamage", target:"opponentBench", amount}`) placed by the interpreter — flat damage to EACH opponent Benched Pokémon (no Weakness/Resistance on the Bench, §8.5); the interpreter only PLACES it (one `DAMAGE_DEALT` per benched Pokémon), the KO check staying in `finishAttack`, so the interpreter still never KOs or touches the flow tail. A sixth deriver sentence recognizes "This attack does N damage to each of your opponent's Benched Pokémon." (optional W/R clarifier). **Web:** the ONLY source change is `projection.ts koParkActiveSeat` treating `resumeTurn` as in-turn (a mid-turn KO park still reports the actor as `activePlayer`); the exhaustive `phaseViewOf` Phase switch is untouched (`resumeTurn` is a PendingStage, not a Phase), and the log/HUD need nothing — `DAMAGE_DEALT`/`KNOCKED_OUT` resolve a benched uid the same way, and the opponent's mid-turn prize pick rides the existing `waitingOn` viewer-follow. Representative demonstrator is a fixture spread attacker (Spread Shot); a live sv card lands with the coverage fan-out. engineVersion 0.7.0. *Why: bench spread/snipe damage (a large card class) and the evolve-below-HP correctness gap both needed the KO target generalized AND a mid-turn KO that resumes the turn — one sweep serving the attack, checkup and mid-turn paths keeps §14 single-sourced, and keeping the KO check out of the interpreter preserves the D23 rule that flow.ts owns every Knock Out.* (2026-07-18) |

| D80 | Half-open sockets are swept with the runtime's OWN keepalive timestamp (P4 online, increment 3c-viii) | The gap 3c-v's browser run surfaced, and the last known way an online match could stall. `setWebSocketAutoResponse` answers the client's 1.5s ping without waking the DO — the thing that makes hibernation worth having — but it also means the DO can never notice pings that STOP. The alternative — dropping the auto-response and stamping `lastSeen` in `webSocketMessage` — was rejected on exactly that ground: it would wake the DO ~40 times a minute per socket and give up hibernation to learn what the runtime already knows. **What it costs instead is a POLL**, because a quiet in-game lobby schedules no alarm at all: `scheduleMaintenance` now pushes a `LIVENESS_SWEEP_MS` (30s) deadline whenever any socket is connected, so an occupied lobby wakes twice a minute. `SOCKET_SILENCE_MS` is 15s — ten missed pings, so a phone changing networks or a throttled background tab is not mistaken for a dead one — and a test pins the budget that matters: sweep + silence + the 5s grace all fit inside the 90s forfeit, so a dead network can never resolve slower than a closed tab. **A `null` timestamp counts as ALIVE**, deliberately: it is the state of every connection before its first ping, and nothing can distinguish "just opened" from "opened long ago and never pinged" — the cost of that reading is a socket we never sweep, versus closing a healthy one-second-old connection. **The sweep only CLOSES**; everything after it — the grace, the seat going disconnected, the forfeit — is the machinery a real close already drives, reached through the same `socketGone` (called explicitly, since a server-side `close()` delivers no `webSocketClose` event to us). 1874 → **1878** tests. **BROWSER-VERIFIED with the very reproducer that exposed the bug:** with a match live, one client was put offline with the socket left open; before this change that produced nothing at all, and now the opponent saw "disconnected — forfeits in 1:30" after ~50s (15s silence + up to 30s sweep + the 5s grace) and the countdown ran. Bringing the client back online restored it within ~10s — the channel reconnected, re-helloed, and the forfeit was cancelled — while the client that stayed connected throughout was never swept. Zero page errors. *Why: the cheapest signal is the one someone else is already recording. Hibernation exists to avoid waking on keepalives, so any fix that inspects keepalives directly is self-defeating; asking the runtime when it last answered turns a per-ping cost into a per-half-minute one.* (2026-07-26) |

  improved iteratively.

## These are defaults, not law
Every decision and assumption here is a **default with a rationale**, chosen with
the context available at the time — revisit any of them when the code or new
context reveals a better path. The point of writing them down is to preserve the
*why*, so a later session can judge whether it still holds.

## Adding / changing a decision
Append a row (or a dated subsection for bigger ones) with the choice **and the
one-line why**. When you revise an existing decision, update its row and note
what changed and why. The one hard rule: **don't reverse a decision silently** —
leave a trail so the reasoning is never lost.

This is that: a nullable `decks.cover_card_id` the editor sets, and a pure **`effectiveCoverCardId(chosen, candidates)`** the list query runs — **the pin wins, and everything else falls through to `pickCoverCardId`**. The derived rule is untouched; it is now explicitly the DEFAULT rather than the answer. **Three decisions carry the slice.** First, **the resolution runs against the candidate list the default was already deriving from**, so honouring a choice costs NO extra query, and a pin that has gone stale (its card removed elsewhere, or its scan gone after a re-ingest) silently falls back instead of drawing a blank rectangle — a deck must never front a card it doesn't run. Second, **the pin may be a TRAINER or an Energy while the derived default stays Pokémon-only**: guessing needs a rule, choosing does not, and a signature Supporter is a legitimate face (browser-verified with Academy at Night, which the rule could never pick). Third, **two fields, deliberately not one**: `DeckSummary.coverCardId` remains the face being DRAWN (so the grid needed no change at all), while the full `Deck` carries `chosenCoverCardId`, the stored CHOICE the editor's picker is set to — null for almost every deck. Collapsing them into one name would have made "what is drawn" and "what was chosen" the same word for two different questions. **`Automatic` is an explicit option in the picker**, not the absence of one, so reverting is one click; it deliberately shows no art, because the default is a RULE and drawing today's answer to it would read as "this card". **The consistency rule lives on both sides:** PATCH validates the pin against the card list the patch LEAVES BEHIND (400 `cover card not in deck`) and drops a pin whose card that patch removes, while the editor's `toSnapshot` drops it locally too — not cosmetic, since the cover rides the same debounced PATCH as the card list, and a self-contradicting body would 400 forever (the saver retries the same dirty snapshot). | D87 | A favourite deck is a validated PIN of the account's OWN deck, resolved on read (P5 polish, increment P5-7) | Joins P5-5 (an editable profile) and P5-6 (a deck's cover art): an account pins one of its own decks as its favourite and sees that deck's cover + name on /settings. A nullable **`users.favourite_deck_id`** (migration `0005`) surfaced as **`userSchema.favouriteDeckId`** — **just the ID.** **Three choices.** First, **store only the id, not the deck's name/cover:** /settings resolves those from the caller's own `GET /decks` list, so a rename or re-cover shows through with no stale copy and a favourite whose deck has vanished resolves to a blank tile — the SAME "derive on read, tolerate stale" the covers use (D83/D86). Second, **a favourite must be one of YOUR decks:** `PATCH /auth/me` gains an OPTIONAL nullable `favouriteDeckId` (absent leaves it, null clears it, a string is validated against the caller's decks) and 400s `favourite deck not found` for anyone else's id or a phantom — the account can never point at a deck it doesn't own, mirroring D86's `cover card not in deck`. Third, **the FK is `ON DELETE SET NULL`** so deleting a favourited deck clears the pin rather than blocking the delete (a RESTRICT FK would) or dangling a stale id; D1 enforces FKs here (the deck DELETE leans on `deck_cards`' cascade), and since drizzle-kit drops the referential action on an ADD COLUMN, migration 0005 restores `ON DELETE SET NULL` by hand. The picker is a native `<select>` in the SAME form as the name, riding ONE PATCH so name + favourite save atomically; the provider adopts the answer, so the corner control follows with no re-probe. 1932 → **1936** tests. Also covered by a DOM round-trip test + schema units. *Why: the profile only needs to REFERENCE a deck, and the deck already owns its name and cover — copying them onto the account would just be a second source of truth to keep in sync; the id plus resolve-on-read is the whole feature, and the validated pin + SET NULL make "your favourite is always a real deck of yours" true by construction.* (2026-07-27) |

| D88 | A card detail view is a read-only modal hydrated on demand from the full-card endpoint (P5 polish, increment P5-8) | Cards in the deck builder had only ever been an add-a-copy tile; this adds a **detail modal** opened from the grid that shows the full card (attacks, abilities, weakness/resistance/retreat, illustrator, rarity, regulation mark, Trainer/Energy rules text). The backend was already complete — a `GET /cards/:id` returning the full `cardSchema`, and a battle-tested `getCard` client — so the whole slice is web-UI; nothing in API/DB/schema/ingest changed. **Four decisions.** First, **the inspect affordance is a SIBLING of the add button, never a child:** the grid tile is a `

+| D89 | Carry `prefers-reduced-motion` through the remaining new-P5 surfaces by appending `motion-reduce:*` variants AT THE CALL SITE (P5 polish, increment P5-9) | Three new P5 surfaces still animated unconditionally, and the app's ONLY global reduced-motion rule (`src/index.css` L190) neutralises just the `<body>` glow transition and the `.route-view` route-fade — it never touches a Tailwind `transition-*`/`scale-*`/`animate-*` utility on a component, so those surfaces were unguarded. An Explore audit found the offenders on `CoverDialog.tsx` (`TILE_BASE`'s `hover:scale-[1.03] active:scale-95`, the close button's `transition-colors`, the Done ghost button), `Settings.tsx` (the font `<select>`, the back-arrow icon's `transition-transform` slide, the Back-to-home ghost button) and `ProfileSection.tsx` (the Save button, the sign-in link); **`PlayerAvatar` was already clean** (its only `style` is a static gradient). Each got `motion-reduce:transition-none` appended, matching the **D88 idiom exactly**: the P5-8 author deliberately patched at the CALL SITE rather than editing the shared `glass.ts` constants, and this slice honours that placement (the alternative — guarding the constants — is written up as the next resume point, see below). **One judgement call:** the Save spinner is a perpetual `animate-spin`, which `transition-none` cannot stop, so it got **`motion-reduce:animate-none`** — the one genuinely-new variant this codebase hadn't used. Two buttons a screen reader announced as "Previous"/"Forward" and that did nothing are worse than none; they are gone. If a real history is built, they come back WIRED. - **The playmat's ⟶ was enabled exactly when the panel covered it** — the panel renders precisely when `passDisabled === false` — so on /play and online it was never clickable. `PlaymatView.onPassTurn` is now OPTIONAL and the control renders only for a driver that passes one: the /simulator sandbox, where nothing covers it.
